newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Equity Bank reports 50 pct rise in yr pretax profit.
newsitem.headline: Equity Bank reports 50 pct rise in yr pretax profit.

text.p: Equity Bank, a unit of NWS Bank Plc and a member of the Bank of Scotland group, on Wednesday reported a 50 percent rise in pre-tax profit to 3.01 million Irish pounds.

The growth reflected a strong performance from the bank's core lending, retail finance and trade finance activities in the Republic and Northern Ireland where its assets have grown in excess of 300 million Irish pounds, chief executive Mark Duffy said in a results statement.
"Equity Bank intends to continue to expand its operations organically and through a greater emphasis on acquisition, joint venture and the development of new products," Duffy said.
Equity Bank said it doubled its gross advances to more than 200 million Irish pounds with average margins of 2.6 percent.
It said its bad debt experience continued to be favourable with the charge for the year of 808,000 Irish pounds reflecting mainly the growth in the general provision.
It said its cost/income rate was 48 percent.
Equity Bank also announced major expansion plans for its telebanking division, Equity Bank Direct, which will create 100 new jobs over the next three years.
It will operate from a separate location following on from a successful pilot study carried out in 1996, the statement said.
Equity Bank Direct provides a direct personal loan service to existing bank customers, affinity groups and captive databases, it said.
